5 Interesting Startup Deals You May Have Missed: Reflecting Sunlight From Space, Better Breathing And Smarter Garbage Trucks

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1576 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Crunchbase

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • This is a monthly column that runs down five interesting startup funding deals that may have flown under the radar.
  • Industry observers note that what if solar farms could keep generating electricity after sunset with a little help from mirrors orbiting Earth?
  • Those are two of the more unusual ideas that attracted startup investment in the past month.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This is a monthly column that runs down five interesting startup funding deals that may have flown under the radar. Check out our previous entry here.

Industry observers note that what if solar farms could keep generating electricity after sunset with a little help from mirrors orbiting Earth? Or researchers could send an experiment into space for less than the price of a car?

Those are two of the more unusual ideas that attracted startup investment in the past month. Our latest roundup also includes a company bringing AI to the old-school business of garbage hauling, another rethinking how factories are programmed, and a consumer brand betting that better breathing could become a major business. Let’s take a closer look.

Solar power has one rather obvious limitation: The sun goes down.

Sources indicate that to that end, Reflect Orbital is working on a solution that sounds straight out of science fiction. The Hawthorne, California-based startup wants to put giant mirrors in orbit to redirect sunlight toward specific locations on Earth, potentially allowing solar farms to keep generating electricity longer after sunset.

Sources indicate that the tech giant recently unveiled $73.5 million in newly introduced funding, bringing its total funding to more than $102 million, per Crunchbase. Existing investors Sequoia Capital, Lux Capital and Starship Ventures participated, alongside new backers including Buckley Ventures, Convective Capital, The Uncommon Group and Salesforce Ventures 1.

Industry observers note that reflect Orbital is developing lightweight, foldable reflectors that it says can be launched aboard satellites and deployed in low Earth orbit. The company envisions using them not only to extend solar power generation, but also to illuminate disaster zones for nighttime search-and-rescue operations or construction sites after dark.

The idea remains unproven in orbit, however. Reflect Orbital is targeting the second quarter of 2027 for its first demonstration mission, which has received FCC approval. The funding will help support those initial introduces, further development of its reflector technology, and commercial partnerships.

The raise comes during a record year for space technology funding. By late August, investors had poured $20.3 billion into space- and satellite-related startups globally, per Crunchbase data, already comfortably exceeding previous annual records.

Nasal strips have been around for decades, but Intake Breathing Technology thinks there’s room for a serious upgrade.

The Santa Barbara, California-based consumer wellness tech giant recently declared a $62 million investment from Camino Partners, the investment platform founded by KIND Snacks entrepreneur Daniel Lubetzky.

In a recent development, intake makes a patented magnetic nasal dilator designed to open nasal passages and improve airflow. Rather than relying on a conventional adhesive strip stretched across the nose, its system uses adhesive tabs and a reusable magnetic band to pull the sides of the nose outward.

In a recent development, the tech giant markets its product to people looking to breathe more comfortably while sleeping, exercising or going about their daily routines. It says it has sold more than 100 million pairs of breathing tabs since 2023, with triple-digit revenue growth over the past three years.

Intake plans to use the newly introduced capital to expand beyond its direct-to-consumer business and into more mainstream retail channels. That’s where Lubetzky’s experience building KIND into a household name could prove useful.

According to recent reports, its funding comes as venture investors show renewed enthusiasm for fitness and wellness. Startups in those categories raised more than $3.6 billion globally in the first half of 2026, putting the sector on pace for its strongest funding year since 2022, Crunchbase data demonstrates.

Recent findings suggest that interestingly, much of this year’s investment into the sector has flowed to wearable devices and health platforms built around AI and data. Intake is a somewhat different bet: a relatively simple physical product that has apparently found a sizable audience without promising to reinvent healthcare through software.

Related Crunchbase query: Global Fitness- And Wellness-Related Startup Funding In 2026.

It has been revealed that taking out the trash isn’t exactly rocket science. But managing the businesses that collect it turns out to be surprisingly complicated.

San Francisco-based TrashLab Software recently raised $12 million in a growth funding round led by Ventana, with participation from existing investors Bienville Capital, Harlem Capital and CreativeCo.

The startup builds an AI-powered operating platform for waste-hauling businesses, an industry where many smaller operators still rely on spreadsheets, paper routes and clunky software to manage their fleets.

TrashLab states its platform combines dispatching, route planning, customer management, billing and payments. Its AI agent, called Haul-E, can answer customer calls and take orders, while cameras in garbage trucks can help document problems such as overflowing dumpsters, blocked containers or bins that weren’t put out for collection.

Sources indicate that the manufacturer says hundreds of waste haulers across the U.S. and Canada now use its software, and that more than 5 million tons of material have been managed through its platform.

It’s not the only startup finding an AI opportunity in the waste industry. We recently covered Greyparrot, a London-based company using computer vision to identify and analyze waste moving through recycling facilities. While Greyparrot focuses on what happens after trash reaches a processing plant, TrashLab is tackling the messy logistics of getting it there.

Related Crunchbase query: Global Venture Funding To Waste Management Startups In 2026.

Factory automation has come a long way, but programming the machines that run industrial production lines can still require specialized expertise and a lot of time.

Gardena, California-based Neuron Industries wants to make the process a lot simpler.

The startup recently revealed a $10 million seed round co-led by FCVC and Obvious Ventures, with participation from Y Combinator, Thin Line Capital, Zee Prime Capital and Founder Factor.

Neuron is developing a fresh kind of industrial controller — the hardware that coordinates sensors, motors and other equipment in factories — alongside AI-powered software that lets engineers describe what they want a machine to do in ordinary language.

Its system generates control code that engineers can inspect, modify and test in simulation before deploying it to real equipment. The goal is to reduce the time and specialized programming knowledge needed to get fresh production lines up and running.

Sources indicate that the startup notes it has already demonstrated its technology on existing factory equipment, including replacing an aging controller on a wood-processing line with roughly three hours of engineering work and eight hours of downtime. It aims to release its Cortex AI Controller commercially in early 2027.

The investment fits into a broader surge in funding for physical AI — technology that applies artificial intelligence to robots, autonomous vehicles, industrial equipment and other machines in the real world. Startups in those categories raised $47.4 billion globally across 521 deals in the first half of 2026, nearly 4x the amount invested in the second half of 2025, according to Crunchbase data.

Related Crunchbase query: Global Physical AI Venture Funding In 2026.

Sending an experiment into space has traditionally required years of preparation, specialized engineering expertise and a very substantial budget.

Austria-based Tumbleweed wants to bring the cost of entry down to as little as 15,000 euros.

Sources indicate that the Vienna startup recently raised 6.9 million euros (roughly $8 million) in seed funding led by PactVC, with participation from Vanagon Ventures, Prototype Capital and EWOR, among other investors. The company describes it as the largest space-tech seed round raised in Austria to date.

Tumbleweed develops standardized containers, called Pods, that allow researchers and companies to conduct experiments in microgravity without building their own satellites or navigating the complex certification process required for space missions.

Customers can place their experiments inside the pre-certified containers, which provide power and communications capabilities while in orbit. The startup handles the logistics of launching the payloads and transmitting experimental data back to Earth.

Industry observers note that unlike many space startups still working toward their first launch, Tumbleweed has already put hardware in orbit. Its inaugural Oasis Alpha satellite rolled out in July carrying experiments for four paying customers, including research into biological processes and space-resource technologies. The mission was fully booked a year before launch.

Tumbleweed says its fresh funding will help it carry out three more missions in 2027 and develop a next-generation spacecraft that would allow customers to bring physical samples back to Earth beginning in 2028.

According to recent reports, tumbleweed is part of a growing European space startup ecosystem, although funding remains concentrated elsewhere. As of late August, European companies had attracted about 10% of global space-tech venture investment in 2026, compared with the more than 60% going to U.S. startups, Crunchbase data indicates.

Related Crunchbase query: Space And Satellite Tech Startup Funding.

Major crypto exchange Coinbase shared the options-implied seven-day ratios for major cryptocurrencies, highlighting that options traders might be preparing for an unusually large price move for XRP.

In an X post, Coinbase Markets shared the outcome of dividing the options-implied 7-day move by the median 7-day move for XRP, Bitcoin, Ethereum, and Solana.

Options-implied 7d move, divided by each asset's own median 7d move: $XRP 1.94× $BTC 1.69× $ETH 1.56× $SOL 1.46× $XRP is priced furthest above its own history, $SOL the least. Which one is asking for more than its own history delivered? https://t.co/WgWbqjcgwI.

It has been revealed that this suggests how much movement options markets are pricing in relative to each asset's own historical behavior. However, it does not compare their expected dollar or percentage moves directly.

Sources indicate that according to the figures shared by Coinbase, XRP's options-implied seven-day move stands at 1.94 times its own historical median seven-day move. Bitcoin follows at 1.69 times, while Ethereum records 1.56 times and Solana comes in at 1.46 times.

XRP, therefore has the highest relative reading among the four assets, suggesting options traders are pricing in a more pronounced move than the token has typically delivered over a comparable period.

In a recent development, at the time of writing, XRP was down 1.93% in the last 24 hours to $0.98 amid the continued profit-taking in the market. XRP briefly reached $1 on November 18, 2026, but fell afterwards as traders took profits. XRP is down 21.57% so far in November, but its history indicates more than its current price action does.

In a recent development, XRP’s average November gain is skewed upward by massive outlier rallies—specifically +550% in 2013 and +282% in 2024. Its median November return is about -10%, meaning it has closed lower in most cycles in history. XRP dropped roughly 23.42% in November 2019 and lost 12.18% in November 2025 (opening at around $2.51 and closing at around $2.20).

A weak November doesn’t always mean a weak December: for instance, after falling 9.1% in November 2015, XRP jumped 46.8% in December 2015.

Sources indicate that in the near term, XRP’s price recovery will target $1 before moving to the $1.24–$1.26 range. Alternatively, if the price falls further, it is likely to find support at $0.89.

Everful, a San Francisco- and Singapore-based startup that connects smaller retailers and brands with Chinese factories and manages the process from order to delivery, has raised $48.5 million in Series A funding.

The round was led by Vertex Ventures Southeast Asia & India and January Capital, with participation from existing investors Square Peg and Lightspeed.

Industry observers note that song, a former Alibaba executive, and serial entrepreneur Kevin Han, who sold a previous company to Amazon, co-founded Everful in 2024. The company began as a jewelry wholesale business before evolving into a multi-category, factory-direct sourcing platform.

In a recent development, retailers and brands often rely on intermediaries, face high minimum order requirements, and experience long sourcing cycles, which tie up capital in inventory before sales trends are clear. Song noticed the growing gap between fast-changing consumer trends and traditional wholesale sourcing models while working as a venture investor at Bessemer Venture Partners, where she mostly focused on cross-border sourcing and meeting numerous startups in the sector. That same gap shaped Everful’s goal to simplify buying directly from factories through an AI-enabled platform.

The B2B sourcing industry is highly competitive. Substantial Tech giant Alibaba connects international buyers with manufacturers and suppliers, while Faire, a San Francisco-based wholesale tech platform, enables retailers to purchase wholesale inventory directly from brands. According to Everful’s co-founders, its key differentiator is responsibility for the sourcing process, rather than simply facilitating transactions.

According to recent reports, “We take care of everything,” Han noted. “We handle sourcing, order consolidation, quality control, and logistics. That’s something the marketplaces don’t offer.”.

Everful is built for smaller retailers and brands without dedicated sourcing teams, Song stated, and it also verifies the factories it works with. While peers also offer services such as quality inspection, logistics, and AI-powered sourcing, Everful aims to integrate these capabilities into a more streamlined purchasing experience, creating an end-to-end process that reduces the work retailers must handle themselves.

Han added that Everful uses AI agents to automate labor-intensive sourcing tasks, including tracking consumer trends, identifying suppliers, coordinating orders across factories, and managing logistics.

Because Everful sources from Chinese factories, ongoing U.S.-China trade tensions and tariffs bear directly on its business. Song stated the co-founders have been thinking about geopolitical concerns since day one of building the organization, and that this has shaped Everful’s strategy from the outset, leveraging her experience at Alibaba and Bessemer Venture Partners.

She mentioned the Trump administration’s suspension of the de minimis exemption, which had allowed eligible shipments valued at $800 or less to enter the U.S. duty-free, as one example of a shift in trade policy.

In a recent development, song explained such changes could favor a model that combines overseas sourcing with local retail sales. “We’re empowering local retailers and brands,” she said. “Long-term cross-border commerce will be cross-border B2B sourcing plus local selling.”.

Everful prepares to use the Series A round to expand its presence in the U.S. and Europe, particularly the U.K., France, and Italy, while investing in AI to automate product customization and other sourcing workflows. It also aims to deepen integrations with e-commerce platforms, building on its Shopify integration as it works toward becoming an end-to-end infrastructure platform for global sourcing.

Sources indicate that the startup employs about 70 full-time staff globally, including 45 in research and development. It has also established an AI operations team to connect engineering and business functions.

On Nov. 18, Hong Kong's Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) added the decentralized exchange Hyperliquid to its list of suspicious virtual asset trading platforms. The listing covers the web interface of the Hyperliquid trading terminal at app.hyperliquid.xyz/trade. The HYPE token dropped to around $65.50 on the evening of Nov. 18, and it recovered to $68.79 by midday Nov. 19, according to TradingView data.

According to the entry, the firm claims to provide digital asset trading services on the website, and it has no address on record. Hyperliquid is not licensed by the SFC, and it is suspected of operating a virtual asset trading platform in Hong Kong or actively promoting its services to the public, the regulator said.

In an accompanying warning, the SFC reminded investors that such platforms often lure owners with "incredible investment opportunities." The SFC also reminded investors that clients of unlicensed platforms have no legal protection if a platform is hacked or misappropriates their assets.

On the same day, the Hyperliquid Policy Center (HPC) sent a letter to the U.K. Financial Conduct Authority with seven recommendations on the country's new crypto rules. "Regulatory obligations belong with persons who have unilateral control over a function that is a regulated activity," the group wrote.

It has been revealed that on Nov. 16, two days before the SFC added Hyperliquid to the list, Hong Kong Financial Secretary Paul Chan spoke at the Bloomberg Global Regulatory Forum. "Before the end of this year, we will introduce a bill to complete the regulatory perimeter," Chan remarked.

According to Chan, the bill will cover crypto dealers, custodians, advisers and asset managers. "Decentralisation does not mean less accountability," he said.

In April, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority licensed HSBC and Anchorpoint Financial as the first stablecoin issuers in the city, out of 36 applicants in the first round.

MIT Review Acclaims zk-SNARKs, but zk-STARKs May Steal the Show

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1248 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nulltx

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Updated look back: this article revisits a 2018 story with what has happened since.
  • In February 2018, MIT Technology Review put zero-knowledge proofs on its list of 10 Breakthrough Technologies under the title "Perfect Online Privacy", and singled out zk-SNARKs as the practical version.
  • The short version: STARKs took a large share of the stage, SNARKs adapted, and Bulletproofs found a narrower job.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Updated look back: this article revisits a 2018 story with what has happened since.

In February 2018, MIT Technology Review put zero-knowledge proofs on its list of 10 Breakthrough Technologies under the title "Perfect Online Privacy", and singled out zk-SNARKs as the practical version. zk-STARKs, published a few weeks earlier, did not replace SNARKs, but they fixed the two weaknesses MIT pointed at and now secure a major Ethereum scaling network.

The short version: STARKs took a large share of the stage, SNARKs adapted, and Bulletproofs found a narrower job. Here is how the three compare and how the story played out.

A zero-knowledge proof lets you prove that a statement is true without showing the data behind it. MIT's examples were proving you are over 18 without giving your birth date, or proving you can afford a payment without showing your balance.

Recent findings suggest that the idea is old. According to ethereum.org, it first appeared in a 1985 paper. What changed was that it became usable. MIT's entry, written by Mike Orcutt, credited much of that progress to Zcash, a currency launched in late 2016, and listed Zcash, JPMorgan Chase and ING as key players.

It has been revealed that the same entry named two drawbacks. zk-SNARKs were slow and heavy to compute, and they needed a "trusted setup". It added that researchers were already looking for alternatives without those problems, but did not name any.

Sources indicate that zk-SNARK stands for zero-knowledge succinct non-interactive argument of knowledge. "Succinct" is the selling point. Zcash's documentation claims a proof is only a few hundred bytes and can be checked in a few milliseconds, even for a very large computation.

Sources indicate that that is what makes shielded Zcash transactions possible. The transaction is encrypted on the blockchain, yet the network can still confirm that it follows the rules.

Recent findings suggest that the cost is the setup. Early SNARKs needed a one-time ceremony that produced public parameters. The ceremony also produced secret randomness, and Zcash's own documentation says anyone who kept it could forge proofs and create counterfeit coins. Zcash ran two multi-party ceremonies, one for its Sprout version and one for Sapling, so that no single person held the secret. Users still had to trust that at least one participant destroyed their share.

The STARK paper, "Scalable, transparent, and post-quantum secure computational integrity", was submitted to the IACR ePrint archive on January 10, 2018 by Eli Ben-Sasson, Iddo Bentov, Yinon Horesh and Michael Riabzev. Its title states the three goals.

Industry observers note that transparent means no trusted setup. STARKs use public randomness, so there is no secret to leak.

Post-quantum refers to the underlying math. Ethereum.org explains that SNARKs depend on elliptic curve cryptography, which a future quantum computer may break, while STARKs rely only on collision-resistant hash functions.

Scalable means the work of checking a proof grows far more slowly than the computation being proved.

Industry observers note that the trade-off is size. STARK proofs are larger, and ethereum.org notes that this makes them more expensive to verify on Ethereum. Figures quoted in the Ethereum Stack Exchange thread that cites this article give a sense of scale: about 288 bytes for a SNARK against about 45,000 bytes for a STARK in one comparison, and "hundreds of kilobytes" in one developer's real project. Those numbers depend heavily on the computation, so treat them as orders of magnitude.

It has been revealed that bulletproofs came out of Stanford in 2017, from Benedikt Bünz, Jonathan Bootle, Dan Boneh, Andrew Poelstra, Pieter Wuille and Greg Maxwell. Like STARKs, they need no trusted setup.

According to recent reports, they were designed for one job: proving that a hidden amount in a confidential transaction falls within a valid range. The Stanford project page notes they cut that proof from over 10 kB to under 1 kB. It also says a Bulletproof takes longer to verify than a SNARK, which is why they are not used for proving large computations.

Monero added Bulletproofs in its October 2018 network upgrade. Its documentation reports that average transaction size fell by at least 80 percent.

It has been revealed that partly. Three things happened after 2018.

It has been revealed that STARKs reached production. Eli Ben-Sasson, the paper's first author, co-founded StarkWare with Alessandro Chiesa and Uri Kolodny. The company used STARKs first in StarkEx, a scaling service for individual clients, and then in Starknet, which launched its Alpha on Ethereum mainnet in November 2021. Starknet's documentation describes it as a permissionless validity rollup that settles on Ethereum using STARK proofs.

Zero-knowledge moved from privacy to scaling. MIT framed the technology as a privacy tool. Its largest use on Ethereum became zk-rollups, which process transactions off-chain and post one proof that they were all valid. Ethereum.org lists Starknet alongside ZKsync, Scroll, Linea, Polygon zkEVM and others. Ethereum.org also puts the cost of verifying a single SNARK on Ethereum at about 500,000 gas and indicates STARKs cost more, which keeps small proofs attractive.

SNARKs fixed their own weakness. PLONK, published in August 2019 by Ariel Gabizon, Zachary Williamson and Oana Ciobotaru, is a universal SNARK: one setup can serve many different programs instead of one ceremony per program. Halo went further. Zcash says Halo removes the trusted setup entirely, and its Orchard shielded protocol, activated with the NU5 upgrade in May 2022, runs on the Halo 2 proving system.

Recent findings suggest that that last point matters for the old "SNARKs need a trusted setup" comparison. It was accurate in 2018. It no longer holds for every SNARK.

Sources indicate that the fair verdict: STARKs did not push SNARKs aside, but they did prove that transparency and hash-based security work at scale. The choice today is less about which family wins and more about what you need: the smallest proof, no setup, or protection against quantum attacks.

Binance will delist five crypto spot trading pairs within the next 24 hours on Nov. 20, 2026, following a review.

To protect its users and to ensure a high-quality trading market, Binance conducts regular reviews of all listed spot trading pairs; it may delist certain spot trading pairs for various reasons, including low liquidity and trading volume.

Binance will delist GAS/TRY, HBAR/BNB, HIVE/TRY, KSM/TRY and ZAMA/TRY pairs on November 20, 2026 at 03:00 UTC, according to an official announcement published on November 18.

Recent findings suggest that four of the five affected pairs are related to the Turkish lira (TRY), while the last one is HBAR/BNB. The decision affects trading between these specific assets and does not mean the cryptocurrencies themselves are being completely delisted from Binance.

The exchange clarified that users will still be able to trade the affected tokens through other available spot trading pairs on its platform.

In a recent development, binance will terminate Spot Trading Bots services for the spot trading pairs simultaneously where applicable. Customers are strongly advised to revision and/or cancel their Spot Trading Bots prior to the cessation of services for Spot Trading Bots to avoid any potential losses.

In a recent development, in related news, Binance Margin will initiate a routine cleanup of Cross Margin accounts with collateral valued at less than 1 USD (or equivalent in other assets), effective from November 30, 2026 at 00:00 (UTC). The cleanup will be executed on a daily basis as an ongoing operational process.

Affected accounts include Cross Margin Accounts with a collateral value of less than 1 USD equivalent across all assets and no outstanding liabilities, as well as Margin Accounts with no capital activity in the past 6 months. Capital activity refers to any action that generates a capital flow.

For each eligible Small-Asset Account, the system will automatically transfer the collateral in owners’ Margin Accounts to their Spot Accounts while the Margin Account functions remain normal, allowing users to transfer, borrow, or trade at any time after the cleanup.

Accounts with collateral equal to or exceeding 1 USD equivalent are not affected by this cleanup.

Home » Exchanges » Trading Bots No Longer a Niche: Now It’s Web3’s Default.

AI-powered trading tools are gradually becoming the default interface for Web3 trading, new research reveals.

A new report from Bitrue Research Institute tracks how trading bots have shifted from specialist software for technical customers into everyday infrastructure across crypto markets.

The research paper combines public GitHub data on open-source projects, a survey of Bitrue owners, and profiles of eight active bots to show where automation is heading.

Industry observers note that public GitHub activity reveals a clear change in focus. Newly introduced repositories describing themselves as “trading agents” jumped from 110 in 2024 to 1,133 in 2025 and reached 6,121 through November 15, 2026, more than five times the prior year’s total.

Classic crypto trading bot projects also grew sharply, rising from 551 in 2024 to 2,399 in 2025 (a 4.4× increase) with another 2,948 created so far in 2026.

The longest-running open-source tools still dominate stars: Freqtrade (56,933), Hummingbot (21,231), Jesse (8,807), and OctoBot (6,951).

An industry survey of 3,708 crypto traders published by MEXC in October 2026 found that 84.8% had used AI for research or trading in the previous six months, with 53.1% doing so at least weekly.

Among AI users, 34.6% had used an exchange’s own strategies or bots and 17.1% had connected an external agent.

On one major multi-exchange platform, average daily bot introduces rose 29% from July to September 2026, reaching 862 per day, with real-fund launches up 36% and DCA bots up 80%.

The report identifies five structural changes:.

In a recent development, in Bitrue’s survey of people who had not yet tried an AI trading bot, concern about losses and risk control was the top reason for hesitation (45.5%). Other common reasons included not trading futures yet (27.3%) and simply not knowing the feature existed (22.7%).

Sources indicate that willingness to let AI trade rose from 55% when only notifications were offered to 71.8% when limits on funds, positions, leverage, and losses were in place. Only 6.5% of respondents said they would allow AI to control more than half their account.

Among non-users, the most requested first steps were a clearer explanation of what the bot does (27.3%) and a trial reward for the first trade (22.7%). Half of those who had not tried an AI bot said they were ready to do so; another 36.4% wanted to learn more first.

In a recent development, users who had already tried Bitrue AI most often cited time saved from watching charts, automatic execution, and market analysis as the main benefits. Requests for improvement centered on more trading pairs, flexible parameters & alerts tied to indicators such as RSI.

The report profiles eight systems that illustrate different approaches:.

In a recent development, AI automation continues to expand, but adoption still hinges on control. Crypto traders want to see why a strategy was chosen, know the maximum loss, test it first, and understand connection security and costs.

Industry observers note that tools that explain their reasoning, enforce user-set boundaries, and allow small or reversible starts are the ones positioned to convert interest into regular use. The report does not forecast specific outcomes beyond these observed trends.

The numbers show both rapid builder activity and cautious but growing trader demand. The gap between the two is being closed by guardrails, explanations, and simpler interfaces rather than by handing full control to AI.

Although XRP is at risk of losing its top-four position in the global cryptocurrency market, the asset still ranks among the three largest crypto assets in Japan.

In a recent post shared by the renowned Ripple-backed XRP treasury firm Evernorth, the organization highlighted XRP’s growing performance in the Japan crypto market.

Earlier today, Evernorth shared monthly data from the Japan Virtual and Crypto Assets Exchange Association (JVCEA) revealing that XRP recorded about ¥132.8 billion in spot trading volume in September 2026.

While this accounted for about 15% of Japan's total crypto spot trading volume during the month, XRP emerged as the third most-traded cryptocurrency in Japan after Bitcoin and Ethereum.

This shows that XRP has outperformed other major altcoins that are at the moment trading in the Japan crypto market, hitting about $880 million in trading volume.

While further data showed Solana and Dogecoin ranking next to XRP on the list as the fourth- and fifth-largest cryptocurrencies in Japan, respectively, the data also showed a wide gap from XRP’s ¥132.8 billion spot volume.

This means that XRP is significantly ahead of Solana and Dogecoin in the Japan crypto trading market, as Solana recorded only about ¥19.47 billion in trading volume during the same month.

Dogecoin, on the other hand, saw less participation, as it recorded only ¥11.27 billion in spot volume during the same period.

With XRP sitting in the third spot, the asset has become one of the most actively traded cryptocurrencies in Japan despite its persistent price volatility.

What’s Coming for Solana in 2027? Upgrade Planned Across Four Key Areas

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. At the 2026 Breakpoint event, Brennan Watt, CEO of Anza, gave a walkthrough of Solana’s wins this year, while sharing what is in store for 2027.

According to Watt, 2026 was a major year for Solana as it migrated its consensus to Alpenglow, slashed the block times in half from 400 ms to 200 ms while doubling capacity.

The Alpenglow upgrade went live on mainnet on October 21, 2026, cutting transaction finality from about 12.8 seconds down to roughly 150 milliseconds. It replaced TowerBFT with Votor, a faster path to reaching agreement.

Sources indicate that after Alpenglow, @bw_solana laid out @anza_xyz roadmap for Solana in 2027 Performance: network compute capacity doubles, transactions cut 80% CU units for token accounts Expressivity: vector processing for models running fully onchain, 64 → 96 accounts per transaction, read account data instead of copying it so less data moves per transaction Market Structure: Alpenglow. Next with faster block distribution and Constellation for clearer ordering rules and more competition among validators Resilience: simpler protocol with fewer special cases, safer to change https://t.co/EpvDdSyjln.

Solana recently transitioned to 1.0, marking the network’s graduation from “mainnet beta” to “mainnet” and retiring the beta designation it has carried since launch. Solana 1.0 recognizes the progress on network performance, resilience, and developer experience.

In a recent development, according to Watt, Solana is eyeing significant improvements in 2027 across four categories. First is Resilience, which involves simplifying the protocol, reducing special cases, and making it safer to change.

According to recent reports, “So, we're going to go ahead and simplify the protocol, replacing legacy abstractions and interfaces, pushing more of the execution on chain, and modernizing some of the wire formats. And all of this, you know, enhances resiliency, but it also allows us to move quicker and be more agile and deploy things and evolve the protocol more quickly,” Watt stated.

Second is Market Structure, which centers on Alpenglow, which aims for faster block distribution, and Constellation, which aims for clearer ordering rules and more competition among validators.

“Several important Alpenglow extensions are coming,” Watt stated. Alpenglow rolls out in two phases: first is Votor, its voting protocol, which is already live on the platform; second is Rotor, a single relay layer planned for a later release that will replace Turbine, the protocol that spreads a block’s data across the network.

In a recent development, third is Performance, where network compute capacity doubles and transactions use 80% fewer compute units for token accounts. Last is Expressivity, which involves vector processing for models running fully onchain and an increase from 64 to 96 accounts per transaction.

Sources indicate that watt also spoke about improvements in onchain development: “The cost of storing data on Solana came down by 27% this year. And just in the coming two weeks, we're going to bring this thing down by another 7x.”.

NEAR’s Inflation Cut: The Math Behind a 5.27% to 3.37% Staking Yield

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1284 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nulltx

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, HSP-029 lowers NEAR’s issuance cap from 2.5% to 1.6% over 24 months.
  • According to recent reports, most headlines on NEAR’s latest inflation schedule stop at “2.5% to 1.6%.” Stakers feel a different number.
  • House of Stake ratified HSP-029 on November 16, after the Security Council’s 14-day veto window passed without a veto.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AI-assisted summary, reviewed by NullTX editors.

In a recent development, HSP-029 lowers NEAR’s issuance cap from 2.5% to 1.6% over 24 months. The cap formula, the epoch step and the yield math show what that does to stakers.

According to recent reports, most headlines on NEAR’s latest inflation schedule stop at “2.5% to 1.6%.” Stakers feel a different number. They earn about 5.27% today and will earn roughly 3.37% once the cut finishes, and a single line of arithmetic accounts for the gap.

House of Stake ratified HSP-029 on November 16, after the Security Council’s 14-day veto window passed without a veto. The proposal touches one parameter, the maximum annual issuance rate, which drops from 2.5% to 1.6% over 24 months. It is the second cut in just over a year, coming after the October 2025 halving from 5%.

Industry observers note that everything else stays put. Issuance still splits 90% to staking participants and 10% to the protocol treasury. There is no upcoming spending program, no validator subsidy and no automatic trigger that could push issuance back up. The full proposal models 11.8 million NEAR of issuance avoided over two years and 66.1 million over six, measured against leaving the cap at 2.5%.

The schedule is a straight line with no stair steps:.

cap(t) = 2.5% − 0.9% × min(t, 24) / 24.

Here t is the number of months since the reduction begins. The 0.9% is the total drop (2.5 minus 1.6), and dividing it by 24 gives a monthly step of 0.0375 percentage points, or 3.75 basis points. The min(t, 24) term caps the ramp at month 24, and the cap sits at 1.6% from there on.

NEAR applies the step every epoch rather than once a month. An epoch lasts about 12 hours, so the cap slips by roughly 0.0006 percentage points each time, far too little to notice on any given day. There are no step dates to mark on a calendar. Sampled every six months, the line looks like this:.

Sources indicate that the yield column uses the math in the next section. It drops about 0.08 percentage points a month, evenly, with no cliff.

Industry observers note that newly introduced tokens go mostly to stakers, so the staked pool splits the reward, and a smaller pool earns more per token. That gives a working formula:.

gross yield ≈ 0.9 × issuance cap ÷ staking ratio.

The 0.9 is the staker share of issuance. Using the proposal’s figures, 0.9 × 2.5% ÷ 0.4271 comes to 5.27%, where 42.71% is the staking ratio reported when the proposal went to vote. Put in the 1.6% cap and 0.9 × 1.6% ÷ 0.4271 gives 3.37%, the same number the proposal publishes. Anyone can check the headline yields on a calculator.

The formula has two limits. It uses the cap, but realized issuance runs a little lower because transaction fees are burned. HSP-029 measured 2.45% in September, which puts today’s yield near 5.16%. The staking ratio also moves. When more people stake, the same rewards spread over more tokens and yield falls further, and when people unstake it climbs. The 3.37% figure assumes today’s ratio holds.

Industry observers note that stakers feel it first. By the proposal’s own math, someone staking 1,000 NEAR ends up with about 20 fewer tokens after two years than if the cap had stayed at 2.5%. The numbers back that up: yield averages about 4.32% across the ramp, roughly 0.95 points under today’s rate for two years.

Holders who don’t stake come out ahead. More than half of NEAR’s supply sits unstaked, and every new token dilutes those holdings. Trimming the cap by 0.9 percentage points trims that dilution by the same amount each year. Stakers give up some reward so that everyone else gives up less value.

Validators get an easier path than in 2025, when the halving cut staking rewards from about 9% to 4.75% in a single upgrade. Operators now have 24 months to proposal. NEAR’s analysis finds that most validator revenue comes from commission on delegated stake, so service quality and fee competition shape income more than the issuance rate does.

It has been revealed that recent history explains the setup. When the 2025 halving shipped, an earlier community poll had missed the two-thirds threshold, and critics mentioned the core team pushed the change through anyway. HSP-029 sidesteps that argument by design.

Two separate approvals are required. Token holders voting through veNEAR set the direction, and that vote closed November 2 with 99.96% in favor and none against. Validators then decide on their own whether to adopt the protocol upgrade that makes the cap binding. The author, Sal Ternullo of SVRN, opened discussion on October 7, and the process ran through the Screening Committee and Security Council in public. Raising issuance again would take a latest proposal and another round of validator adoption, so nothing can be added quietly later.

Sources indicate that ratification does not change issuance yet. A one-quarter grace period comes first, giving wallets, exchanges, custodians and staking providers time to upgrade their disclosures. NEAR One then releases the upgrade and validators choose whether to adopt it, with the reduction starting about a quarter after ratification. On schedule, that means a start in early 2027 and a 1.6% cap around early 2029.

Three things are worth tracking. Validator adoption of the upgrade comes first, because the cap stays at 2.5% until enough validators run it. The staking ratio comes next, since it moves yield regardless of the formula. Last are the quarterly transparency reports NEAR has promised, which compare realized issuance with the schedule.

Price is a separate question. Lower issuance eases supply pressure, but nothing in it creates demand. The cap will follow its published line down, and yield will follow the cap.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • According to Glassnode’s recent revision, publicly listed Bitcoin miners have sold nearly half of their Bitcoin holdings since January 2026.
  • This means that miners are increasingly treating their Bitcoin reserves as a source of liquidity to fund business operations and maybe for expansion into AI data centers.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that as 2026 is nearing its end, Bitcoin [BTC] miners are facing growing financial pressure. This, in turn has resulted in miners increasingly selling their Bitcoin reserves instead of holding them for long-term appreciation.

According to Glassnode’s recent revision, publicly listed Bitcoin miners have sold nearly half of their Bitcoin holdings since January 2026.

This means that miners are increasingly treating their Bitcoin reserves as a source of liquidity to fund business operations and maybe for expansion into AI data centers.

It has been revealed that at the same time, there is also a decline in transaction fee revenue. With 11 months into 2026, Bitcoin miners earned just 912 BTC in transaction fees, the lowest annual total since at least 2011. This is a huge drop compared to 1,720 BTC in 2025 and 15,178 BTC in 2024.

Recent findings suggest that in other words, transaction fees accounted for only 0.63% of total miner revenue in 2026, down from 1% in 2025 and 6.5% in 2023. This is enough proof that demand for Bitcoin block space has weakened, reducing the contribution of this revenue source.

Remarking on the same, CleanSpark CBO Harry Sudock mentioned,.

Like with any commodity production business, it should get harder and thinner margin over time because the lowest cost operators should be the most successful and durable.

In other words, Sudock believes Bitcoin mining will become increasingly competitive over the next decade, with shrinking profit margins favoring operators with the lowest production and electricity costs.

He expects the global hashrate to continue growing, but at a slower pace than in the previous ten years, as mining hardware becomes more efficient and large publicly listed miners explore AI data centers.

He also argued that Bitcoin mining will not depend solely on large public companies, as smaller businesses and privately held miners can operate profitably.

In a recent development, at the same time, CryptoQuant CEO Ki Young Ju noted that Bitcoin’s average mining cost reached approximately $62,862 in Q3 2026, based on Marathon Digital’s filings. With BTC trading near this level, miners are facing shrinking profit margins and could face potential losses if prices fall further.

However, the relatively high hashrate suggests miners remain committed to the network despite growing profitability concerns.

This comes as Bitcoin miners are shifting their focus towards AI and high-performance computing (HPC), as investors increasingly value their power infrastructure and data centers.

Companies such as Core Scientific, IREN, and TeraWulf are generating significant revenue from AI infrastructure and HPC services, in some cases surpassing their Bitcoin mining income.

However, the Miner Outflow chart suggests that compared with the rest of the year, November outflows are calm.

At the same time, the Miner Reserve chart was at about 1.1925 million BTC at press time. In fact, through October and into November, it moved in a narrow band, roughly between 1.192 million and 1.1926 million.

All in all, miners are roughly holding steady, with small accumulation or lower net selling.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Home » Bitcoin (BTC) » Bitcoin Is Calmer Than 19% of S&P 500 Stocks, But Here’s a Catch.

Grayscale’s latest report highlights a hidden risk that still catches market-timing investors off guard.

Upcoming research from Grayscale shows Bitcoin’s (BTC) volatility has fallen to roughly 43%—lower than nearly one in five S&P 500 stocks.

Industry observers note that the catch? Bitcoin’s calmer day-to-day trading hides a massive trap for anyone trying to time dips: almost all of its multi-year gains still come from just a handful of explosive trading days.

Recent findings suggest that in its report, “Beyond Volatility: Rethinking Cryptocurrency Risks,” US digital asset manager Grayscale says Bitcoin’s long-term performance is heavily influenced by a handful of trading days. Its returns have “fat tails,” meaning sharp gains and losses occur more frequently than in traditional stocks.

Industry observers note that over the past three years, Bitcoin delivered an annualized return of roughly 60%. Excluding its 10 best days would have cut that figure to 7%, while excluding its 10 worst days would have raised it to 197%.

The report also notes that Bitcoin has historically rebounded sharply after major declines. Since 2011, it has experienced seven drawdowns exceeding 50%, although Grayscale says these declines are not unusually severe compared with stocks and bonds when adjusted for volatility.

Grayscale also sees Bitcoin as a potential portfolio diversifier because it is less exposed to traditional market factors.

The company points out that Bitcoin has historically recovered sharply after significant declines. Since 2011, Bitcoin has experienced seven drawdowns of more than 50% from previous highs.

Recent findings suggest that the report cites Bitcoin’s inclusion in J.P. Morgan Asset Management’s 2027 Long-Term Capital Market Assumptions as a milestone.

Grayscale describes JPMorgan as a $5 trillion investment manager that now examines Bitcoin alongside established asset classes.

Recent findings suggest that the banks’ 10-year base case for Bitcoin projects a 10% compound annualized return for Bitcoin over the next decade, the highest among the asset classes covered. The forecast also assumes 55% annualized volatility and a 33% correlation with US large-cap stocks, the number below international equities, corporate bonds and hedge funds.

In Bitcoin’s early years, volatility routinely exceeded 100% and at times approached 200%, with a market cap in the single-digit billions.

Grayscale ties the decline to roughly 43% to larger market value and liquidity, greater institutional participation, Bitcoin exchange-traded products and regulatory clarity.

In historical tests, modest Bitcoin allocations raised annualized return and Sharpe ratio in a representative institutional portfolio.

Over three years, Bitcoin explained about half of return variation across FTSE Grayscale Crypto Sectors. Among the 10 largest non-stablecoin assets, six led quarterly performance over the past two years, while Bitcoin led none.

Recent findings suggest that JPMorgan’s decision to include Bitcoin in its long-term forecasts, along with declining volatility, could shape how institutions approach crypto investments. At the same time, Grayscale’s data indicates how much Bitcoin’s long-term performance depends on a small number of trading days, highlighting the risks of trying to time the market.

This means ordinary investors can now buy up to 300,000 rubles ($3,700) in a year through a single broker, exchange, or asset manager, after passing a mandatory test.

However, qualified investors are not subject to such asset limits and trading restrictions.

The development points out that Russia has taken decisive action to deepen the integration of the crypto market with traditional finance. The debut indicates surging retail interest in cryptocurrency amid regulatory evolution.

It has been revealed that it signals a strategic shift in how traditional exchanges handle digital assets. Accommodating retail clients signals growing confidence in the crypto market’s maturity. This highlights rising demand for coordinated exposure to crypto assets within Russia’s capital markets.

The announcement introduces upcoming entry gateways that give retail investors organized access to the crypto market, redefining how these assets are traded locally and internationally.

In the past, crypto in Russia operated in a highly restrictive, complex regulatory environment. Now, the regulator is moving toward a balance between investor freedom and financial stability. In July, the central bank opened the door to crypto for companies to facilitate global trade. This month, it introduced new legislation that allows retail investors to trade crypto within specified limits.

This decision comes after over a year of regulatory filings and multiple delays.

Sources indicate that as per the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) filings on Nov. 18, Roundhill has officially withdrawn prepares to launch the Roundhill XRP Covered Call Strategy ETF and Roundhill Solana Covered Call Strategy ETF.

Interestingly, it submitted the applications for these two funds on Oct. 17, 2025. Therefore, these two funds had been awaiting launch for over 13 months.

As per the latest regulatory filings, Roundhill has been consistently delaying the effective dates for these two funds.

However, instead of launching them, the investment firm has decided to drop both products.

In its requests to withdraw the filings for these funds, Roundhill revealed that it "has no further intention to pursue effectiveness of the Fund." The firm noted that it had not sold any shares under the registrations for these two funds.

Intriguingly, Roundhill failed to elaborate on the sudden decision to axe its prepares to launch these two ETFs.

Sources indicate that roundhill was planning to launch income-generating XRP and Solana ETFs using a covered call strategy. In such a strategy, investors sell options to earn premiums while also maintaining exposure to the price movements of XRP and Solana.

Unlike spot-based ETFs, these funds would not have held the cryptocurrencies directly. Instead, they would have used options written against existing cryptocurrency ETFs.

In a recent development, A covered call strategy can be useful for generating regular income. However, it can also cap profits during strong market rallies.

Notably, there has been relatively low demand for income-generating cryptocurrency investment products. This raises concerns about investors' interest in these ETFs.

Surprisingly, this decision came amid substantial net inflows into spot-based XRP and Solana ETFs.

Industry observers note that U.S. spot XRP and Solana ETFs recorded net inflows of roughly $969 million between May and October 2026, according to data from SoSoValue.

Overall, these spot ETFs held around $3.26 billion in assets under management as of the end of October.

Cryptocurrency exchanges operate by acting as a connecting platform between buyers and sellers. They provide users with a trading platform to create accounts, complete their KYC, deposit and withdraw funds, and start trading in the supported cryptocurrencies.

Industry observers note that customers can access features like spot, futures, and derivatives trading. There are wallets available that allow them to store, deposit, and withdraw digital assets. Crypto exchanges make markets accessible to individuals and institutions around the world and provide liquidity. Here is our list of the top 9 crypto exchanges of November 2026:.

Binance was established in 2017 and is one of the biggest crypto exchanges in the world. It has evolved into one of the most comprehensive ecosystems that caters to retail investors, developers, and institutional customers.

In a recent development, it has a lot of trading services, including spot, margin, futures, and peer-to-peer trading in supported markets. There are also advanced charting tools, trading indicators, various order types, and market analysis that support different types of trading.

Recent findings suggest that founded in 2017, OKX has developed a broader ecosystem over time that includes Web3 services, derivatives, cryptocurrency trading, and blockchain-related products. The platform is a great pick for retail owners, and professional traders alike.

It has the options of spot trading, margin trading, futures, and perpetual swaps. There are market charts, technical indicators, order management features and tools that are designed for amateur and experienced traders.

It has been revealed that kraken was founded in 2011 and is one of the oldest exchanges in the space. It supports cryptocurrency buying, selling, and spot trading while the Kraken Pro platform has advanced trading options that include market charts, order books, technical analysis and different order execution options.

There are margin trading, futures, staking options also available on the platform. They have a strong focus on security which includes measures like encryption, account protection features, two-factor authentication, and secure digital asset custody arrangements.

In a recent development, bitget has spot and futures trading along with other digital asset trading options. It has real-time market information, technical charts, trading indicators, and order management features. Copy trading is one of its major distinctive products that lets owners replicate trading strategies from other traders on the platform.

In a recent development, there are security measures like withdrawal controls, risk monitoring and asset protection mechanisms in place to ensure user safety. They also support a lot of crypto and trading pairs letting consumers access to different digital asset markets.

In a recent development, kuCoin has a wide range of cryptocurrencies and trading services and provides traders access to digital assets, spot trading, margin trading, and futures. There are trading charts, technical indicators, multiple order types, trading charts and market information.

Industry observers note that there are also trading bots available that allow users to automate selected trading strategies. Lending-related products, and wallet integrations are also part of the KuCoin platform.

It has been revealed that crypto.com was established in 2016 and created a broad ecosystem over the years that includes cryptocurrency trading, payments, digital wallets, and other blockchain-related products. It also has a crypto wallet, payment-related products and eligible digital asset earning programmes.

Sources indicate that the security measures on Crypto.com include multi-factor authentication, withdrawal protection, digital asset custody controls and account monitoring. The exchange is also known for its customer-oriented approach and efforts to connect crypto services with everyday financial activities.

Bitfinex offers margin trading, spot trading and derivatives products along with lending and funding related services in supported markets. There are detailed order books, customizable trading layouts, advanced charts and multiple order charts.

Industry observers note that the advanced trading interface and liquidity infrastructure distinguish it from platforms designed primarily for beginners. In terms of security measures as well, Bitfinex has monitoring mechanisms in place and multi-factor authentication as well.

Coinbase started out in 2012 and has developed its services beyond cryptocurrency buying and selling to include institutional custody, and many blockchain-related products that are useful for advanced and beginner users. It was created with the vision of making crypto accessible through a secure and user-friendly digital platform.

The platform has an Advanced trading experience that lets traders use features such as real-time market charts, order books, price indicators, and advanced order execution options. Coinbase Prime gives eligible institutions access to trading, custody, and other digital asset infrastructure.

Gate supports a wide range of digital assets and crypto trading pairs. Its ecosystem has options like spot trading, margin trading, futures trading, digital asset management, Web3 services, and derivatives.

Gate supports 5,400 digital assets and has over 63 million customers around the world with lightning-fast listings for latest and trending tokens.

Recent findings suggest that crypto exchanges are an essential part of the global financial system and important towards driving mainstream crypto adoption. Exchanges connect individuals, businesses, institutional investors and financial markets and aren’t just trading platforms but also enablers of digital adoption.

As with any financial decision, owners should conduct their own research, review an exchange’s security measures and fee structure, and fully understand the risks involved before committing significant funds.

Ripple's RLUSD stablecoin led the daily ranking of stablecoin inflows into decentralized finance (DeFi), according to Token Terminal data that RWA Foundation shared on X. The DeFi total value locked (TVL) of Ripple's stablecoin grew by $22.3 million over 24 hours, and Tether added $21.6 million. RWA Foundation titled its chart "Ripple led stablecoin DeFi growth.".

Paxos, Open Standard and Societe Generale followed with $7.8 million, $4 million and $1.2 million, respectively. World Liberty, United Stables, MetaMask, Tori and Liquity each added less than $700,000 over the same period.

In a recent development, about $2.8 billion worth of RLUSD is in circulation, compared with about $180 billion worth of Tether's USDT. Tether's stablecoin is still more than 60 times bigger than RLUSD.

In a recent development, ripple released RLUSD in December 2024. In mid-September 2026, RLUSD supply passed $2.44 billion, and about $1.38 billion of it was on Ethereum. About $1.05 billion was on the XRP Ledger, Ripple's home network. On Ethereum, the stablecoin is used in DeFi pools on Aave V3, Curve and Morpho.

RLUSD is issued by Standard Custody & Trust under the supervision of the Newly introduced York State Department of Financial Services (NYDFS), and its reserves are held at custodian bank BNY. In the fall, RLUSD received a Moody's rating and was listed on Coinbase and Robinhood, and Ripple received final approval from the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) to launch Ripple National Trust Bank.

Ripple has also integrated RLUSD with payment providers Arf, Convera and Cross River Bank, and the stablecoin is now used in dollar settlements between companies.

In a CNBC interview on Nov. 19, Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse called blockchain-based transactions "a wave of emerging technology." "I think 10 years from now you'll see blockchain implemented across our financial infrastructure," he said.

An Ethereum [ETH] Foundation-linked wallet has dumped 6,700 ETH since Friday, the 13th of November, according to Lookonchain data.

In a recent development, the blockchain analytics firm also observed that four whale-linked wallets withdrew 13,408 ETH in recent hours. Even so, the ETH price was down 0.5% in the past 24 hours and 11.95% over the past week.

It has been revealed that according to SoSoValue data, U.S. Ethereum spot ETF flows totaled -$77.23 million as of the 16th of November. This week’s ETF outflows reflected bearish sentiment in the market.

Sources indicate that yet, the exchange ETH reserves were also dropping alongside the price. AMBCrypto reported that the low reserves could help set up a Q3-style rally.

Analyst CryptoOnChain reported that the 7-day average Ethereum reserve on Binance was 2.97 million ETH. This reading put it in the 1st percentile of the past year, with a Z-score of -2.79.

The 7-day average Binance USDT reserve was $29.71 billion, which was once again in the 1st percentile of the past year, with a Z-score of an even more astonishing -3.37.

It has been revealed that the values meant that, compared to the past year, the ETH, and USDT reserves were at an annual floor. The Z-score drew further attention to the anomaly; readings beyond ±2.0 are major statistical outliers.

The analyst also noted that the outflows were concentrated on Binance, as all-exchange flows of ETH were only down 2.1% in a month, compared to Binance’s 11.3% drop.

Industry observers note that it is possible that the Binance ETH outflows were going toward self-custody or staking. The record staking numbers reflected long-term investor belief despite recent price losses.

Lowered stablecoin reserves also indicated reduced buying power on Binance. Overall, the falling stablecoin and ETH reserve were a cautious combination, but the next price move’s direction is not yet confirmed.

Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin’s push to position ETH as a store of value was another hopeful sign for long-term investors.

Strategy reportedly sold 32 BTC in June, followed by three larger sales in July and August.

Earlier sales coincided with its cost basis falling below the $75,400 average cost level.

Its latest reported purchase was 485 BTC on November 16, as the average cost line came under pressure again.

Strategy could be approaching another shift in its Bitcoin strategy. Historical data from BitcoinTreasuries reveals several sell-offs when its average cost line was breached. Now, its raising questions about whether the latest dip could interrupt its buying streak.

The organization’s last reported purchase was 485 BTC on November 16. But with the average cost level back in focus during November, investors have a reason to watch its next move.

The historical figures show four reported sales: 32 BTC on June 1, 3,588 BTC on July 6, 1,637 BTC on August 3, and another 1,691 BTC on August 10.

Recent findings suggest that that’s a notable sequence. It suggests the average cost line may have coincided with previous changes in the manufacturer’s buying and selling activity.

Purchases reportedly resumed in September after the average cost level was regained. That buying continued into November, with the latest recorded purchase standing at 485 BTC on November 16.

Now the average cost line has reportedly been breached again. That puts the latest purchase under scrutiny. If the earlier pattern repeats, the November 16 acquisition could prove to be the last buy before another period of selling.

The possibility is worth watching, but history isn’t a guarantee. The data figures show past sales and a recurring relationship with the $75,400 average cost level; they don’t confirm a rule requiring Strategy to sell Bitcoin whenever that level is crossed.

For now, Strategy BTC sales remain a possibility rather than a confirmed next move. The next purchase disclosure will matter. If no fresh buying appears, investors may start asking whether the November 16 purchase marked the end of this accumulation phase.

Home » Trendsetter News » XRP Tackles $1.07; Broader Downtrend Still Looms.

XRP could rebound toward $1.06–$1.07 as tentative signs of a bottom emerge, according to Cilinix.

In a recent development, XRP may have room to recover toward $1.06 and $1.07, according to the host of Cilinix Crypto, whose latest XRP analysis points to tentative signs of a bottom. The forecast is conditional: renewed weakness in equities could instead send the token back toward $0.90 and $0.85.

The distinction matters. The host sees enough improvement to support a short-term rebound, but not enough to call an end to the larger downtrend. “The higher timeframe structure is still very bad,” the analyst stated.

According to recent reports, the technical argument rests partly on XRP reclaiming its seven-day rolling volume-weighted average price, or VWAP, after a period of declines. The host noted that earlier recoveries above that measure had preceded upward moves, while cautioning that the indicator does not always carry much significance.

Sources indicate that XRP had also moved back into the developing monthly value area, with an initially favorable reaction. Together, those developments gave the analyst more confidence that the market could stabilize and gradually push higher.

According to recent reports, there is a weakness in that setup, however. XRP broke above a previous swing high but promptly fell back below it and had not reclaimed it at the time of the analysis. The host described that part of the structure as “slightly bearish.”.

In a recent development, funding rates offered another supporting signal. They turned sharply negative around the recent lows before becoming positive again, which the analyst viewed as consistent with a potentially defended bottom, not confirmation of a lasting reversal.

The broader backdrop kept the host cautious. Oil prices remained low and the volatility index had opened lower, but the S&P 500 was still near its lows.

Cilinix also cited a lack of ETF inflows as one reason not to adopt an XRP outlook that ran against the wider market.

It has been revealed that the $1.06–$1.07 area is therefore a potential recovery zone, not a confirmed breakout target. Cilinix would become more conservative there because of the weak higher-timeframe structure.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Solana has remained one of the major cryptocurrencies that have been heavily affected by the persistent crypto market volatility, stalling demand from both retail and institutional investors.

While Solana has continued to struggle amid the growing market uncertainty, it appears that traders are increasingly exiting their positions even across its DeFi market.

Recent data showcased by blockchain monitoring platform Lookonchain shows that two Solana whales unstaked a total of 2.31 million SOL on November 19.

While the total amount of SOL unstaked was worth about $169.4 million, further data demonstrated that the whales proceeded to transfer the tokens to Coinbase, a leading cryptocurrency exchange in the U.S.

It is important to note that the act of withdrawing SOL previously committed to the network's staking mechanism is regarded as unstaking.

While this move automatically gives holders the ability to transfer, sell, or use the unstaked tokens, the massive unstaking of 2.31 million SOL from large holders has drawn attention within the crypto community regarding the intention behind the move.

With curiosity on the rise about the whales' decision to move such a large amount of SOL to Coinbase Prime, the timing of the move has triggered speculation that the whales may be intending to sell the tokens.

Notably, the move arrived when Solana was trading around $74, briefly shifting into green territory just a few days after it retested $67, the lowest level seen since June 2026.

Since the prolonged price correction has continued to weaken investor confidence, it appears that the whales have acted upon the growing fear and withdrawn the assets they had initially committed to the Solana network to hedge against further losses.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • It has been revealed that six days after Jensen Huang resigned as CEO of the firm he co-founded 33 years ago, Nvidia delivered the best quarter in its history.
  • Fourth-quarter guidance came in at $130 billion against the $125.3 billion Wall Street wanted, with China assumed at zero.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Morning Minute is a daily newsletter written by Tyler Warner. The analysis and opinions expressed are his own and do not necessarily reflect those of Decrypt. And check out our daily news show 'FOMO HOUR' covering all of the top stories and market action.

🖥️ Nvidia Beats, Board Notes ‘No’ on Jensen.

It has been revealed that six days after Jensen Huang resigned as CEO of the firm he co-founded 33 years ago, Nvidia delivered the best quarter in its history. And told him he isn’t coming back.

Fourth-quarter guidance came in at $130 billion against the $125.3 billion Wall Street wanted, with China assumed at zero.

And the CFO raised their 2028 revenue outlook to 75% year-over-year growth.

Just an absolute smash all around.

Then board chair Harvey Jones got on the call and noted it plainly. “The Nvidia board does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.” The directors unanimously accepted his resignation, and Jones declined to answer anything about the circumstances or the independent investigation still running.

Huang had publicly offered to come back hours earlier, saying he would do it if directors believed it served shareholders and employees. Trump and Elon Musk both backed the idea. A petition passed 182,000 signatures including nearly 9,000 self-identified Nvidia employees. None of it moved the room.

It has been revealed that nvidia has hired Heidrick & Struggles to run the permanent search. Colette Kress stays interim CEO while remaining CFO, with Jones saying the board has “every confidence in Colette’s leadership, integrity and ability to deliver.” The board also created a National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee, chaired by director Suzanne Nora Johnson, to receive reports from the company’s national security and trade compliance teams.

And after all of that—the stock rose about 3%.

Industry observers note that A 6% revenue beat, guidance $5 billion above consensus, a new product cycle shipping, and the market gave it two percent. Shares sit roughly 35% below their October peak near $240. Nvidia perps on Hyperliquid were doing nearly a billion dollars of daily volume through the week, bouncing off $150 before settling near $162.

As for impact on the broader AI trade, Nvidia proved AI demand is not collapsing. You cannot manufacture $107.6 billion of data center revenue, and margins at 74.8% mean nobody is discounting to move product. The demand-collapse thesis died on Tuesday.

Two details do belong to the bears though. Growth is decelerating from 103% to roughly 77% once you strip the extra week out of Q4 guidance. And gross margin guides down about three points, from 74.8% to between 71% and 72%. Slowing growth plus compressing margins is how multiples come down regardless of how major the absolute numbers get.

It has been revealed that the honest read is that the AI business is fine and the AI trade has stopped responding to it. For crypto that matters more than it should, because the correlation that dragged Bitcoin from $87,000 to the low $60s over six weeks ran through this exact trade.

Now we wait for the Fed on December 9 and insight into the 2027 rate hike cycle (or lack thereof) to determine the likely near-term fate.

  • Notably, the agency also warned that a significant decline in their market value could erode Tether’s reserve surplus and potentially leave it undercollateralized.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

S&P Global Ratings assigned a score of 5 to Tether’s USDT, the weakest in its five-point stablecoin stability scale. What’s more surprising here is the fact that the assessment, which was published on the 18th of November, 2026, has remained unchanged since November 2025.

This was mainly because there was a growing proportion of higher-risk assets in Tether’s reserves. According to S&P Global, these assets accounted for 28% of circulating USDT as of the 30th of September 2026, compared with 24% in 2025.

Notably, the agency also warned that a significant decline in their market value could erode Tether’s reserve surplus and potentially leave it undercollateralized.

Sources indicate that that said, Tether’s reserve composition has also shifted over the past year, with gold holdings rising from $12.9 billion in September 2025 to $19 billion in September 2026. Meanwhile, the company also added $4.2 billion in publicly traded equities, while its Bitcoin holdings declined from $9.9 billion to $8.4 billion.

Yet, despite the growing exposure to riskier assets, Tether reported $191.45 billion in reserves against $183.50 billion in liabilities as of the 30th of September. This in turn left a reserve buffer of approximately $7.95 billion and a collateralization ratio of 104.3%, up from 103.9% in 2025.

Still, above all of this, USDT traded close to its $1 peg over the past year, while its market capitalization grew from $158 billion to approximately $184 billion between September 2025 and September 2026.

However, according to a recent AMBCrypto report, Tether’s market capitalization dropped by $6.6 billion over the course of sixty days, ending on the 7th of November.

Ripple’s Brad Garlinghouse Notes Crypto Markets Could Rebound After Anthropic Goes Public

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse believes the recent crypto market sell-off stems largely from investors rotating capital into high-profile initial public offerings.
  • Speaking to CNBC on November 19th, Garlinghouse drew a direct parallel to SpaceX’s public debut earlier in the year.
  • The same pattern, he remarked, unfolded ahead of Anthropic’s offering.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse believes the recent crypto market sell-off stems largely from investors rotating capital into high-profile initial public offerings. The Ripple boss and crypto billionaire anticipates a recovery once Anthropic’s massive listing is fully absorbed.

Speaking to CNBC on November 19th, Garlinghouse drew a direct parallel to SpaceX’s public debut earlier in the year. He explained that when major IPOs generate intense demand, investors often sell liquid assets such as Bitcoin and XRP to free up cash for share subscriptions.

The same pattern, he remarked, unfolded ahead of Anthropic’s offering. After SpaceX completed its listing, crypto markets staged a notable rebound. Garlinghouse expects a similar bounce this time.

Anthropic, the artificial-intelligence manufacturer behind the Claude chatbot family, has priced its IPO at $83 per share, above the previously marketed range of $70 to $78.

The deal ranks among the largest IPOs in history, raising tens of billions of dollars and valuing the manufacturer in the trillion-dollar range, and shares are set to begin trading on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT.

Such blockbuster offerings typically attract enormous institutional and retail interest, temporarily diverting capital from other risk assets. Once the primary allocation is complete and secondary-market trading stabilizes, some of that capital often flows back into crypto and other liquid markets.

In a recent development, bitcoin had slipped near $62,000 on Wednesday before recovering above $63,000 early Thursday. Garlinghouse framed the dip as a temporary capital-rotation effect rather than a fundamental loss of confidence in digital assets. He also expressed confidence that Anthropic’s shares would trade strongly given the strong demand and pricing above the range.

Looking further ahead, Garlinghouse remained optimistic about blockchain’s long-term role. He predicted that within roughly a decade, blockchain technology will be deeply embedded across global financial infrastructure, much as artificial intelligence has already transformed multiple industries.

His comments highlight how large technology IPOs can create short-term pressure on crypto while potentially reinforcing longer-term narratives around innovation and capital markets.
